title: An execution-oriented NetOps benchmark: generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline evaluation (provisional preregistration, adapter-hosted execution)
research_question: Does an execution-oriented benchmark that integrates LLM generation, deterministic validators, simulator enactment, and automatic rollback scoring (pipeline C) reduce the actionable misconfiguration rate by at least 30% relative to a generation-only baseline (pipeline A) on a representative public/synthetic NetOps confirmatory task set?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Pipeline C (generate→validate→simulate→rollback) yields a lower actionable misconfiguration rate than pipeline A (generation-only); target = ≥30% relative reduction.

H2: A constraint-based validator (pipeline B) and a formal-verifier+simulator pipeline (pipeline C) produce statistically distinguishable reductions in actionable misconfigurations when paired within tasks.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do reductions vary by task cluster (routing, ACL, NAT)?
EQ2: How sensitive are primary results to model choice within the single supplied-execution-model constraint (primary execution model vs internal seed variability)?
EQ3: What are validator false-positive rates and their operational tradeoffs (prevented enactments vs unnecessary blocks)?
benchmark_scope: Public network-configuration corpora and curated deterministic synthetic variants derived from: Open network-configuration corpus (https://openalex.org/W4392875514), NetOps public examples (https://openalex.org/W4405935382), and dataset provenance collections (https://openalex.org/W7125775240).
Deterministic topology/intent perturbations generated from pre-registered augmentation seeds [42, 123, 999] (scripts and hashes released with artifacts).
primary_estimand: The paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion per task between pipeline C and pipeline A (P_actionable_A - P_actionable_C), measured across N=160 confirmatory tasks (paired per task across conditions).
secondary_estimands: Paired difference between pipeline B and A.
Validator false-positive rate (fraction of tasks where validator blocks a configuration that simulator would not flag as actionable).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory tasks = 160. Construction: ingest public records from benchmark_scope; filter to vendor-neutral, non-proprietary examples; deterministically augment selected items with topology variants using augmentation seeds [42, 123, 999]. Task clusters: routing (~64 tasks), ACL (~64 tasks), NAT/other (~32 tasks). Exact snapshot script, input hashes, and selection order are published with artifacts. Exclude tasks requiring proprietary vendor-OS commands or unsupported constructs.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion across N=160. Target effect: relative reduction of ≥30% in actionable misconfiguration rate. Detectable absolute difference estimate: with conservative baseline p=0.30 and N=160, SE_diff ≈ 0.0512; 95% CI width ≈ 0.100 → detectable absolute difference ≈ 10 percentage points. Thus the pre-registered target (30% relative reduction ≈ 9 percentage points when baseline=30%) is near the detectable limit with N=160. Bootstrapped CIs (10,000 replicates) will be used for final inference and reported precisely.
exclusion_rules: Exact duplicate prompt/config hash -> automatic exclusion from confirmatory pool and replacement by next eligible seeded variant.
Tasks requiring proprietary vendor/OS commands or unsupported dialects -> exclusion and documented counts.
Any task failing the transformation validation unit tests -> exclusion from confirmatory analysis and reassignment to discovery logging.
missingness_plan: If a model API call fails (provider error, network timeout), automatic retry up to 2 times; persistent API failure for a task-method-seed combination is logged as technical failure. Missing model outputs due to persistent provider failure are excluded from the paired comparison for that model/pipeline only; all exclusions and counts reported. No manual imputation will be performed.
analysis_plan: Primary metric: actionable misconfiguration (binary per enacted config) as detected by deterministic simulator safety checks. Primary analysis: paired bootstrap (10,000 replicates) on per-task binary outcome to estimate 95% CI for the paired difference (A minus C) and compute two-sided p-value for H1. Report absolute and relative reductions, bootstrap CI, exact p-value, and numbers-needed-to-protect. Secondary analyses: paired contrasts B vs A and C vs B, cluster-specific descriptive results. Multiple comparison adjustments for secondary families via Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (α=0.05). Report validator false-positive rates and severity distributions. All code, seeds, and raw outputs published.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: C vs A only (one primary contrast). Secondary contrasts (C vs B, B vs A, subgroup tests) are secondary/exploratory and corrected via Benjamini–Hochberg within those families. All permutations and corrected p-values reported.

stopping_rule: Pre-registered stopping rule: complete the full confirmatory run of N=160 tasks; no early stopping for outcomes. Technical aborts only on infrastructure or regression-test failures; such events are logged and re-scheduled under the frozen retry policy and overall model-call budget limits.
planned_outputs: Raw model outputs and prompt logs (per-task, per-seed).
Simulator enactment traces and safety-violation labels.
Logged validator blocking decisions and reasons.
Analysis scripts, bootstrap outputs, and reproducible figures/tables.
Dockerized simulator and parser/canonicalizer code with hashes.
